title: R’ Yonatan ben HaMeshullam
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Yalkut, Matot](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Torah.785.19), on “On the day he hears,” cites [Sifrei Zuta](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Zuta.30.14.1): R’ Eliezer ben Yaakov says: “Once I asked Yonatan ben Meshullam and Yehoshua ben Gamla. They told him that R’ Akiva said—and when I came to R’ Yehoshua,” etc. Hyman says scribal errors have occurred in these names in several places.[^4]

[Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1873&lang=en) records that R’ Yose testified in the name of his brother Yonatan, who spoke in the name of R’ Elazar Chisma. Hyman says the intended passage is [Gittin 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.62a.3-4), where our text reads R’ Yochanan. At the beginning of [Tosefta Demai, chapter 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Demai.3.1), the reading is R’ Natan.[^5]

notes.text: The checked Sifrei Zuta explicitly says Eliezer ben Yaakov, whereas Gittin 62a says Elazar ben Chasma. The two ר״א expansions therefore differ. Hyman’s “they told him” inside the first-person account remains a compressed source anomaly.

The saved whole Leipzig1917 Sifrei Zuta30:14:1 scalar explicitly has Eliezer ben Yaakov, Yonatan ben Meshullam and Yehoshua ben Gamla; its later related account has Yehoshua ben Memel. The first reads אמרנו, we said, and the later אמרו לי, they told me, against supplied אמרו לו, they told him. These forms remain distinct, without assigning their origin to Yalkut or Hyman or proving scribal history. Heading ben HaMeshullam remains distinct from body ben Meshullam. פ״א is ONCE, not chapter1. Hyman’s several-place scribal-error claim and Seder HaDorot brother-report/Yochanan/Natan variants remain attributed. Eliezer here differs from the earlier Gittin Elazar Chisma comparison. All named personal titles in this saved scalar are abbreviated; full Rabbi is not inferred from the metadata.

The consulted Yalkut Shimoni, Torah 785, has אמרו לי, “they told me,” and names Yehoshua ben Gamla in both tellings. The Leipzig Sifrei Zuta has “we said” in the first and “they told me” with Yehoshua ben Memel in the second. Hyman’s print confirms “they told him” in his quotation. Seder HaDorot gives Yonatan as the brother in the transmission, Gittin 62a gives Yochanan, and Tosefta Demai 3:1 gives Natan. These are the readings of those witnesses; the differences do not by themselves settle the person’s identity or the history of the wording.

The linked Yalkut has “they told me” in both replies and gives Gamla in both places. The linked Sifrei Zuta gives Gamla in the first exchange and Memel in the second. It reads “we said” in the first reply and “they told me” in the second. The translation retains Hyman’s quotation in the body.

[Heilprin’s entry on Yose](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1913&lang=en) explicitly compares Yonatan with Yochanan in the received text. The linked Tosefta names Natan. These witnesses give different names in the chain.
